gaps.sentence: Had I ___ the risks, I would never have invested.
gaps.explanation: After inverted 'Had I', the past participle follows: known.

gaps.sentence: He always carries a power bank in case his phone ___.
gaps.hint: in case plus the present simple
gaps.explanation: 'In case' takes the present simple for things that might happen: dies.

gaps.sentence: If she were more organised, she ___ the deadline last week.
gaps.explanation: A present unreal cause with a past result is a mixed conditional: would not have missed.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ me tonight, I will send you the files first thing.
gaps.explanation: A realistic future condition uses the present simple after 'if': email.

gaps.sentence: I will tell her the news when I ___ her at the party.
gaps.hint: when clauses take present for future
gaps.explanation: Time clauses with future meaning use the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: Unless the road ___, the coach cannot use this route.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' takes the present simple, here in the passive: is widened.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ late again, the manager will have to speak to you.
gaps.hint: a warning about a real future
gaps.explanation: A real warning about the future keeps the if-clause in the present simple: are.

gaps.sentence: ___ harder, she would have passed the exam.
gaps.hint: inversion replaces if in formal English
gaps.explanation: Formal English can drop 'if' and invert: Had she studied harder, she would have passed.
